messages:
jordan: Hey team - running a POC with an APAC customer (SG-based legal team). They want explicit proof that for the POC: 1) inference requests stay in asia-southeast1, 2) logs/metrics can be restricted/short retention, and 3) a list of any subprocessors that would hold customer data (with country/region). Can we assemble a small evidence bundle?

matt: Quick clarifying Q - is this Hosted demo or Dedicated capacity?

jordan: Hosted, using our singapore region. They keep asking 'no cross-border sync' and need a simple network/flow diagram + a subprocessor CSV with storage regions. Also want a CAIQ snippet on encryption in transit+at rest.

suren: We can do that. For hosted: inference and KV cache run in asia-southeast1, but operational logs by default land in our central logs store unless we scope them. Options: disable verbose logs for the POC, redact PII, and set retention to 7 days. We have CAIQ answers for crypto controls (TLS 1.2+, AES-256 at rest, KMS-backed keys). I can export: (A) regional network/flow diagram, (B) subprocessor manifest with region column, (C) excerpted CAIQ responses for related domains.

julie: From DPA/legal side: we can add a POC-limited clause restricting subprocessors to SG/SEA for the duration and require notice before adding anything outside region. If customer insists on HSM/KMS in their tenant, we can discuss Private deployment but that’s a heavier lift.

presales-bot: presales-docs: uploaded -> https://redwood.internal/presales/POC-SG-evidence-bundle (regional-POC-evidence.pdf, subprocessor-manifest.csv, caiq-encryption-extract.md) :file_folder:

matt: attaching quick ASCII flow to use in the deck:

```
Client (app in SG) -> TLS -> Edge (asia-southeast1) -> Inference runtime (asia-southeast1) -> Optional KV cache (asia-southeast1)
                           
Logs (redacted) -> Log aggregator (configurable: SG or central)
Storage for artifacts (model+cache snapshots) -> GCS asia-southeast1 (default)
```

jordan: Customer asked specifically about 'who touches raw request payloads' — can we confirm ops staff don't have plaintext access?

suren: Operations don't routinely access raw request payloads. We redact PII from logs by default for hosted customers; for extra assurance we can enable automatic request payload redaction and limit retention. For the POC I can attest to: no support access to raw requests without documented approval, and we can add an audit trail.

jordan: perfect. Can you also confirm subprocessors and where they store backups? Customer legal wants the backup location column in the CSV.

suren: Done — subprocessor-manifest.csv in the bundle includes columns: name, role, services, primary-region, backup-region, contact. Top entries: GCP (Cloud Storage/Compute) - primary: asia-southeast1, backup: us-central1; Managed Redis (cache) - primary: asia-southeast1; CDN/edge provider - regional. Note: some compliance metadata (e.g., vendor SOC2 links) also included.

julie: I'll prepare a one-paragraph DPA addendum for the POC limiting subprocessor regions + 7d retention and no-PII support access. Jordan — want me to send to their counsel or attach to our SOW?

jordan: please send to their counsel and cc me. timeline?

suren: I'll hand over the finalized PDF bundle + signed manifest by EOD today.

jordan: awesome, thanks all :thumbsup: will follow up with customer once I have the bundle.
